summary: One of six Prince Albert National Park towers; the first five date to 1938 and all were decommissioned in 2001. Cupola is at the Waskesiu museum; site today unknown.

facts.design: Cupola on a tower, with a one-room cabin and pit privy at its base

events.note: Museum dates the first five park towers to 1938; Sanctuary falls in that group on the list. No Sanctuary-specific date found.
Museum says the park's fire towers were decommissioned in 2001 and replaced by helicopter smoke patrols.

evidence.supports: park network of six fire towers, Sanctuary among the named towers
evidence.quote: Prince Albert National Park at one time had a network of six fire towers which played an important role in fire suppression.

evidence.supports: tower person watches for smoke from the tower
evidence.quote: Once in the tower, the person spends the day watching for smoke or signs of smoke.
Blue Bell (The first 5 were constructed in 1938.)

notes_for_editor: Record coordinates (54.17139, -106.47361) match the websiteservice position 54-10.2833 X 106-28.4167 (decimal minutes); no correction. The 1938 build date is the museum's date for the first five park towers; Sanctuary is in that group by list order only, not by a stated date, hence medium. The date the cupola was taken down is not given, so no removed event. Site today unknown: no source found. A Waskesiu museum Facebook post titled 'This fire tower on Sanctuary...' could not be read (login wall; fetch_text and WebFetch returned only the title), so it is not cited. Parks Canada culture page and the historicplaces Grey Owl page were read and had no tower text. The expansion candidate file lists 'Santuary' as another spelling; not used. The websiteservice Prince Albert section photo captions dated March 21, 1991 are not used. Design and staffing facts describe the park network as a whole, per the museum. Two web searches and six page reads used.
